text:
Open Desk: who's the most underrated creative in Kurdistan right now? Illustrator, photographer, calligrapher, anyone.

Name them below and tell us why. We'll start following.

slides.title: What happens in our first call.
slides.body: No pitch deck. No sales script.

slides.title: You talk. We listen.
slides.body: Where you are, where you want to go, what's in the way.

slides.title: We ask the awkward questions.
slides.body: Who exactly is this for? What would you never do?

slides.title: We tell you what we'd do.
slides.body: An honest first opinion, even if it's not what you expected.

text:
A first conversation with 33 Studio costs you nothing but an hour. Here's what to expect.

33studio.org

Before anyone rented desks by the month, Slemani had tea houses: one small table, two strangers, and a glass that never stayed empty for long. Plenty of good ideas in this city were first argued over tea.

Which tea house is yours?

slides.title: The best brands look like where they're from.

text:
Our streets, our script and our humour aren't something to hide behind a generic look.

They're the advantage. The most interesting brands of the next decade will look like where they're from.
A sketch goes in the bin once we've decided it isn't the one. Keeping the bin means nobody spends next week arguing for an idea we already tested and dropped.

slides.title: Made in Sulaymaniyah. Made for anywhere.
slides.body: A creative agency from Kurdistan, for brands with bigger plans.

text:
Great brands don't need to come from a capital city. They need a point of view and people who care about the craft.

We're both. 33studio.org
Every autumn the market stalls fill with pomegranates, split open so you can see the red inside. If a brand owned that colour for a season, people would remember it.

Kurdish, Arabic and English don't share a direction, a baseline or a rhythm. Drawing them together from the first pencil line is how a bilingual brand avoids looking translated in two of its three languages.

slides.title: Why we killed it: it needed a caption to work.
slides.body: If an idea needs explaining, it isn't finished.

text:
Kill List is where we share ideas that didn't make it, and why.

This one was beautiful and confusing. Beautiful is easy. Clear is the work.

To every student in Slemani with a sketchbook open at 3am and a deadline at 9: the habit of caring this much about one curve or one colour is exactly what clients end up paying for. Get some sleep when you can.

Ask any AI tool for a logo and you'll get something competent in seconds. So will your competitor. Competent is about to cost nothing; what still costs money is the decision that makes a brand recognisable, like the colour nobody else would pick or the line only you would say.

That's the work we do. 33studio.org

slides.title: Same logo everywhere?
slides.body: Signs, social, invoices, uniforms. All the same version.

slides.title: Can you say it in one sentence?
slides.body: What you do, and why it matters.

slides.title: Does it still fit?
slides.body: Your brand should be as ambitious as your business.

text:
Most brands don't need a revolution. They need someone to notice what's quietly not working.

Take the check.

Slemani Type, part one.

Long before fonts arrived on a computer, shop names in this city were painted by hands that knew the letters. Some of those signs are still up, faded and beautiful.

Seen one we should photograph? Tell us the street.

Right-to-left isn't a problem to solve. It's a rhythm to design with.

The page reads differently. So should the design.

Some ideas are clever and still wrong for the brand. They're the hardest to drop, because everyone in the room likes them.

If you've ever deleted your favourite draft, you know the feeling.
Taste isn't what you like. It's what you're willing to say no to.

If an idea needs a screen, three fonts and a render before it makes sense, it isn't ready yet. Draw it on whatever is on the table. When the person across from you gets it in five seconds, it's worth building.

slides.title: Sell the building before the first brick.
slides.body: 3D renders, films and branding for new developments.

text:
Buyers can't walk through a building that doesn't exist yet. With 3D renders and a brand worth believing, they can picture living there.

We help developments sell early. 33studio.org

slides.title: What did you make this week?

text:
Open Desk: post something you made this week in the replies. A sketch, a photo, a layout, a half-idea.

We'll look at every one.
Drive up to Goyzha around sunset and the city turns into layers of hills, haze and the first lights coming on below. Every designer in Slemani has a photo like this somewhere on their phone.

Nobody at the spice stall put turmeric next to sumac because a mood board said so. They put it where customers would see it, and it still looks better than most brand palettes.

Next time you're in the bazaar, look at the stalls the way a designer would.

Thank you to everyone who replied, argued, shared and showed us their work this month.

You're the culture we keep talking about.

Which Kurdish word is the most beautiful to look at, not just to say?

We're asking for a reason.

Studio note: the best feedback this week came from someone who isn't a designer.

They didn't know the rules. They knew what they felt. Listen to those people.

slides.title: Your brand has a voice. Does it sound like you?
slides.body: Bilingual copy and tone of voice.

text:
Most brands look designed and sound improvised.

We write how your brand speaks, in Kurdish, Arabic and English, so every caption sounds like the same person. 33studio.org

Trends travel fast now. A look that starts somewhere else arrives here within a week.

The brands that last aren't the fastest to copy. They're the ones worth copying.

Kurdistan has illustrators, photographers and calligraphers doing work that would hold up anywhere, and too few walls and screens to show it.

Tag one creative whose work more people should see. We'll go and look at every name in the replies.
